historical_context: Tenali Ramakrishna was a 16th-century Telugu poet, scholar and advisor in the court of King Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara Empire. Known for wit, humor, intelligence.

stories.title: Tenali Raman and the Theft of Wells
stories.full_story: One summer Vijayanagara faced water shortage. Tenali noticed wells drying not from drought but because palace guards stole water at night for merchants. Tenali placed chilies in one well, guards caught drinking that water were identified by red eyes, king punished them.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Two Thieves and the Royal Treasure
stories.full_story: Two thieves boasted they could steal king's treasure. Tenali let them steal fake treasure chest filled with bees, thieves beaten by bees and caught.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Three Dolls
stories.full_story: King Krishnadevaraya received three identical dolls from a foreign king who asked which is most valuable. Courtiers failed. Tenali inserted wire through dolls: first wire came out mouth (talks too much), second came out ear (hears but doesn't retain), third came out heart (retains wisdom). Third doll most valuable.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Horse Trader
stories.full_story: A trader sold a weak horse claiming it was fast as wind. King bought. Tenali told trader to ride horse and chase wind, trader fell, exposed fraud.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Cat and the Milk
stories.full_story: King's mother worried about mice, asked to guard milk. Tenali brought a cat, but cat drank all milk. Tenali said cat is like greedy officials who guard wealth but steal.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Dream of Palace
stories.full_story: A courtier claimed he dreamed king gave him 1000 gold. Tenali said he dreamed courtier gave him 1000 gold in return. King laughed and made courtier pay.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Brinjal Curry
stories.full_story: Tenali loved brinjal curry, his wife made excellent. King loved it too and forbade anyone else growing brinjals, keeping all for palace. Tenali secretly grew brinjals on terrace, wife leaked aroma, king smelled and caught Tenali but forgave after witty excuse.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Golden Mango
stories.full_story: A miserly courtier never shared mangoes from his garden. King wanted one. Tenali told miser king would cut mango tree if he didn't share, miser brought mangoes. Tenali distributed to all, saying sharing increases sweetness.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Great Pundit
stories.full_story: A haughty pundit from Kashi challenged Vijayanagara scholars, claimed title Tilakashta Mahisha Bandhana. Tenali broke the phrase: Tila = sesame, Kashta = firewood, Mahisha = buffalo, Bandhana = rope. He showed firewood tied with buffalo rope - sesame? Actually Tila-kashta... No book exists, just firewood tied with buffalo rope. Pundit was actually carrying firewood tied with rope on head, exposed as fool, fled.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Thieves and the Well
stories.full_story: Thieves hid gold in well. Tenali told owner to worship well, thieves thought owner knew and moved gold, were caught red-handed.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Weight of Cotton
stories.full_story: A merchant cheated with false weights. Tenali asked him to weigh cotton vs iron same weight - merchant's trick exposed because cotton looked more but weight same.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Horse of Two Colors
stories.full_story: King's horse had two colors, artist couldn't paint. Tenali made horse roll in mud, made it one color, artist painted, then washed horse - trick.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the List of Fools
stories.full_story: King asked Tenali to make list of fools in kingdom. Tenali wrote king's name first because king believed horse could lay eggs after trader fooled. King laughed, asked Tenali to add his own name if horse didn't lay egg.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Justice of the Parrot
stories.full_story: A merchant left parrot to watch shop. Thief came, parrot screamed, Tenali caught thief. King made parrot court bird.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Arabian Horse
stories.full_story: Arab trader brought fine horse for 5000 gold. Courtiers jealous said horse lame. Tenali proved horse fine by riding blindfolded - horse avoided obstacles by instinct.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Crows and the Scarecrow
stories.full_story: Farmer complained crows ate crops. Tenali placed scarecrow that looked like king, crows feared king, left crops. Farmer rewarded.

stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Goddess Kali
stories.full_story: Young Tenali went to Kali temple, goddess appeared with bowl of curd and bowl of knowledge, asked choose. Tenali tasted curd then said why not both, goddess laughed and granted wit. Later he became poet in King Krishnadevaraya court.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Painting of the King
stories.full_story: King asked painters to paint him. One painted king taller, one shorter. Tenali painted king with eyes closed hunting - king liked because it hid one blind eye without insult.

stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Challenge of the Silent Pot

stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Tax Collector

stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Greedy Priest
stories.full_story: Temple priest took all offerings. Tenali gave him statue that leaked offerings back to poor through hole, priest caught.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Magic Mango Tree
stories.full_story: Tenali planted mango seed and said mantra 'I am fool' - tree grew quickly? Actually story where Tenali tricks guards that mango tree grows if you confess foolish act.

stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Tale of the Missing Gold

stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Cure for the King's Cold
stories.full_story: King had cold, doctors failed. Tenali made king laugh so much with joke that cold cleared with sneezing.

stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Persian Scholar

stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Donkey and the Washerman
stories.full_story: Washerman's donkey lost, Tenali found and painted stripes like tiger, washerman feared, Tenali revealed trick to teach not to neglect donkey.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: Tenali and the Dream Merchant
stories.full_story: A man sold dreams. Tenali bought dream of being king for 1 gold, next day claimed half kingdom because in dream he was king.
stories.moral: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
stories.source: Folklore - Vijayanagara Empire 16th century, public domain

stories.title: The Price of Buttermilk
stories.full_story: Old woman sold buttermilk for 1 coin, courtier demanded free. Tenali made courtier churn buttermilk himself all day, understood labor.

stories.title: The Two Brothers and the Field

stories.title: Tenali and the Woodcutter's Axe
